name: Spokeo, Inc. v. Robins
summary: The Court held that a plaintiff alleging violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act must show a concrete — not merely technical — injury, even when Congress has created a statutory cause of action, remanding the case for further analysis.
significance: Spokeo established that a concrete injury cannot be satisfied by a bare procedural or technical statutory violation alone, and is a foundational precedent for Paramount's argument that Salazar needs more than a VPPA breach to establish standing.
